intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the largest ancient castle complex in the world, including St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Walk through centuries of Bohemian history with stunning panoramic views over Prague's red rooftops.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most iconic thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. Experience the unique Hungarian bathing culture that has been a city tradition for over 150 years.

experiences.name: Old Town Prague & Astronomical Clock Walking Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the medieval Old Town Square, witness the famous 15th-century Orloj Astronomical Clock chime on the hour, explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov), and discover Gothic, Baroque, and Romanesque architecture layered across centuries.

experiences.name: Buda Castle Hill & Hungarian National History Walk
experiences.description: Climb or take the historic funicular up Castle Hill to explore Buda Castle, Matthias Church, and the Fisherman's Bastion. Discover over 1,000 years of Hungarian royal history with breathtaking views across the Danube to Pest.

experiences.name: Danube River Evening Cruise with Budapest Illuminations
experiences.description: Sail along the Danube at dusk and witness Budapest's UNESCO-listed riverscape light up at night, including the illuminated Parliament Building, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle. A magical way to appreciate the city's architectural grandeur from the water.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight LH lands at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the airport bus (Line 119) to Nádraží Veleslavín metro station, then metro Line A to Malostranská or Hradčanská stop. Check into your Hradčany district boutique stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation Walk around Hradčany: Stroll along Hradčanské náměstí (Hradčany Square), admire the Schwarzenberg Palace exterior, and walk down Nerudova Street to get your bearings. Peek into the Castle District gates (free to enter the courtyards) and enjoy panoramic views over the red rooftops of Malá Strana and the Vltava River.
day_by_day.evening: First Dinner & Sunset at Prague Castle Ramparts: Walk to the southern garden terraces of Prague Castle for a free golden-hour view. Then head to Malostranské náměstí (Lesser Town Square) for dinner at a local pub.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a pastry/coffee at the airport before landing — budget ~€3
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the hotel after check-in: try a local pekárna (bakery) for an open-faced chlebíček sandwich and juice — budget ~€4
meals.dinner: U Kocoura pub on Nerudova Street — traditional Czech svíčková (beef sirloin) or goulash with bread dumplings and a half-liter of Czech beer — budget ~€8–10

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 24-hour public transport pass (€3.60) at the airport. September in Prague is mild (15–20°C), bring a light jacket for evenings. Exchange a small amount of cash to Czech Koruna (CZK) — cards are widely accepted but local pubs often prefer cash.

day_by_day.morning: Prague Castle Complex: Purchase the Prague Castle Circuit B ticket (~€8) covering St. Vitus Cathedral, Old Royal Palace, and the Basilica of St. George. Arrive early (9:00) to beat crowds. Climb the Great South Tower of St. Vitus for sweeping city views. Explore the Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička) — tiny colorful houses once home to castle guards and artisans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Malá Strana & Charles Bridge: Walk downhill through Malá Strana's baroque streets. Visit the Church of St. Nicholas (entry ~€2). Cross the iconic Charles Bridge (free) lined with 30 baroque statues — read the legends. Continue into Staré Město (Old Town) and explore the narrow lanes around Týn Church.
day_by_day.evening: Old Town Square & Astronomical Clock: Watch the Orloj (Astronomical Clock) chime at the top of the hour — free spectacle. Climb the Old Town Hall Tower (~€6) for a dusk panorama. Wander the square as street musicians play.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre-style morning at a local kavárna near the hotel — coffee and a croissant or párek v rohlíku (hot dog) from a street stand — budget ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Lokál Malá Strana: a beloved Czech canteen-style restaurant — order svíčková or roast pork knee with sauerkraut and a Pilsner Urquell — budget ~€7–9
meals.dinner: Restaurace U Parlamentu or a similar Old Town budget spot — try řízek (Czech schnitzel) with potato salad and a local Kozel dark beer — budget ~€8–10

day_by_day.notes: The Castle Circuit B ticket is the best value combo. Go early to avoid tour groups. Charles Bridge is most atmospheric at dawn or dusk — plan your crossing accordingly. Keep CZK cash for small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Josefov (Jewish Quarter): Explore the historic Jewish Quarter on foot. The combined Jewish Museum ticket (~€16) covers six synagogues including the Old-New Synagogue (Europe's oldest active synagogue) and the haunting Old Jewish Cemetery with 12,000 graves layered over centuries. A deeply moving and historically rich experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wenceslas Square & National Museum: Walk to Nové Město (New Town). Stroll down Wenceslas Square — a historic boulevard, not a square — site of the 1968 Prague Spring and 1989 Velvet Revolution. Visit the National Museum (€6) at the top of the boulevard, recently renovated with excellent exhibits on Czech history and natural science.
day_by_day.evening: Vyšehrad Fortress at Sunset: Take the metro to Vyšehrad station. Walk to this lesser-visited hilltop fortress with free entry to the grounds. Stroll the ramparts for dramatic views of the Vltava, visit the Vyšehrad Cemetery (burial place of Dvořák and Smetana), and watch the sun set over the river.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh pastries and kávička (coffee) from a local pekárna near the hotel — budget ~€3
meals.lunch: Lehká Hlava (Clear Head) — a popular vegetarian restaurant near Josefov with affordable lunch specials — budget ~€7–8
meals.dinner: Hospoda Na Schodech near Vyšehrad or a local neighborhood pub — try bramboráky (potato pancakes) or smažený sýr (fried cheese) with tartar sauce, a Czech classic — budget ~€6–8

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter is emotionally intense — allow 2–3 hours and go at your own pace. Vyšehrad is far less touristy than the Castle and offers some of Prague's best free views. Wear comfortable walking shoes — today covers significant ground.

day_by_day.morning: Letná Park & Holešovice District: Cross the river and climb to Letná Park — free, beloved by locals for jogging and cycling. Find the giant metronome (site of the former Stalin statue) for stunning panoramic views over Prague's bridges and Old Town. Explore the trendy Holešovice neighborhood with its street art, indie cafés, and the DOX Centre for Contemporary Art (€6).
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Budapest: Head to Praha hlavní nádraží (Prague Main Train Station) and board a RegioJet or FlixBus to Budapest. The train takes ~6.5 hours; book in advance for prices as low as €15–25. Depart around 13:00–14:00. Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside en route.
day_by_day.evening: Arrival in Budapest & District VII Exploration: Arrive Budapest Keleti station around 19:30–20:30. Take the metro (Line M2) to your accommodation area. Drop your bags and take a short evening stroll through the Jewish Quarter (District VII) — Budapest's vibrant ruin bar district. Pop into Szimpla Kert (Kazinczy utca 14) — the original ruin bar, free entry, a must-see cultural institution.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area café or grab lángos (fried dough with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor near the train station — budget ~€2–3
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for the train: grab fresh bread, local cheese, salami, and fruit from a potraviny (corner shop) near the station — budget ~€4–5
meals.dinner: Kádár Étkezde in Budapest's District VII — a legendary, no-frills Hungarian lunch/dinner spot beloved by locals — try gulyás (goulash) or töltött káposzta (stuffed cabbage) — budget ~€6–8

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest transport at least 2–3 weeks ahead for best budget prices on RegioJet (regiojet.com) or FlixBus. The train is more scenic and comfortable than the bus. Budapest uses Hungarian Forint (HUF) — withdraw cash at a bank ATM on arrival, avoid exchange booths at the station.

day_by_day.morning: Buda Castle Hill & Matthias Church: Take the metro and then walk or take the historic Funicular (€3 one way) up Castle Hill. Explore the free Royal Palace grounds and the Hungarian National Gallery (free on Saturdays). Visit Matthias Church (€5) with its stunning geometric Zsolnay tile roof. Walk the Fisherman's Bastion (free outer terraces) for iconic panoramic views of the Danube and Pest skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Crossing the Danube — Pest Side Exploration: Walk across the Chain Bridge (Lánchíd) — one of Budapest's most iconic structures. Explore the elegant Belváros (Inner City) district. Visit the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — free to enter, a stunning 19th-century iron hall packed with paprika, local produce, folk crafts, and affordable food stalls on the upper level.
day_by_day.evening: Hungarian State Opera House & Andrássy Avenue: Walk up the grand Andrássy Avenue (a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard). Admire the neo-Renaissance State Opera House exterior — or book a budget evening tour (~€10) if available. End the evening at a ruin bar or along the Danube Promenade watching the illuminated Parliament building across the water.

meals.breakfast: Espresso Embassy or a local cukrászda (pastry shop) — try kürtőskalács (chimney cake) or rétes (strudel) with coffee — budget ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Great Market Hall upper floor food stalls — lángos with toppings, or a plate of goulash soup with fresh bread — budget ~€4–6
meals.dinner: Frici Papa Kifőzdéje — a beloved Budapest institution for cheap, hearty Hungarian home cooking — try pörkölt (meat stew) with nokedli (egg dumplings) — budget ~€6–8

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is lively in Budapest — markets and streets are busy. The Fisherman's Bastion is free on weekdays and mornings; a small fee applies on weekend afternoons (€3) but the Chain Bridge view is free anytime. September evenings can be cool — bring a layer.

day_by_day.morning: Hungarian Parliament Building & Kossuth Square: Join a guided tour of the Hungarian Parliament — one of Europe's largest and most beautiful parliament buildings. Tours run throughout the day; book online in advance (~€8 for EU citizens, €18 for non-EU). The interior is breathtaking — gilded halls, the Hungarian Holy Crown, and sweeping Danube views. Explore Kossuth Square and the surrounding neoclassical architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi: Take the metro (M1 — the continent's oldest underground railway) to Széchenyi Thermal Bath in City Park. Purchase a cabin/locker entry (~€20–22) and spend 2–3 hours soaking in the iconic yellow neo-baroque outdoor and indoor thermal pools. A quintessential Budapest experience. Afterward, stroll through Városliget (City Park) — free — and see Vajdahunyad Castle (free exterior).
day_by_day.evening: Heroes' Square & Ruin Bar Night: Walk to Hősök tere (Heroes' Square) — a grand UNESCO-listed plaza with the Millennium Monument and statues of Hungarian chieftains — free. Return to District VII for dinner and an evening exploring the ruin bar scene: Instant, Fogas Ház, or Ellátó Kert are all free-entry, atmospheric options.

meals.breakfast: Sunday morning at a local pékség (bakery) — fresh kifli (crescent rolls), vaj (butter), and a strong kávé — budget ~€2–3
meals.lunch: Light snack before the baths — grab a langos or sandwich from a street vendor near Keleti — budget ~€3–4
meals.dinner: Bors GasztroBar — a cult-favorite Budapest spot known for creative soups and sandwiches at rock-bottom prices — long line but worth it — budget ~€5–7

day_by_day.notes: Book Parliament tours online at least a day ahead (látogatokozpont.parlament.hu). Bring flip-flops and a towel to Széchenyi (or rent towel for ~€2). The M1 metro (yellow line) is a heritage railway — a historic ride in itself. Sunday in City Park is wonderful — locals picnic and relax.

day_by_day.morning: Dohány Street Synagogue & Jewish Quarter History: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street — the largest in Europe and second largest in the world. Entry ~€12 includes the Hungarian Jewish Museum and the moving Holocaust Memorial Garden (Tree of Life sculpture). Explore the surrounding District VII streets with their mix of Art Nouveau buildings, memorial plaques, and vibrant café culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gellért Hill & Freedom Monument: Take a tram or walk to the base of Gellért Hill and hike up (free, ~20 minutes) to the Citadella fortress and the Freedom Monument — a Soviet-era statue now recontextualized as a memorial. The views from the top are arguably Budapest's best — a 360° panorama of the entire city, both Buda and Pest, and the Danube with all its bridges.
day_by_day.evening: Danube Evening Cruise or Riverside Walk: For a budget alternative to paid cruises, walk or cycle along the Pest bank of the Danube at dusk — the Parliament, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle are all illuminated magnificently. If budget allows, a basic evening boat cruise runs ~€10–12 and lasts 1 hour. End the night with a farewell Hungarian dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square — a Budapest institution since 1858; splurge slightly on a coffee and slice of Dobos torte (~€5–6) — worth it as a cultural experience
meals.lunch: Hummus Bar on Király utca — generous portions of hummus, falafel, and pita bread at excellent prices — budget ~€5–6
meals.dinner: Menza Restaurant on Liszt Ferenc tér — retro communist-era aesthetic with modern Hungarian cuisine; try the Hungarian fish soup (halászlé) or beef goulash — budget ~€10–12 (slight splurge for a memorable last Budapest dinner)

day_by_day.notes: Gellért Hill hike takes about 20–30 minutes up a paved path — wear good shoes. The Danube riverside walk at night is completely free and utterly magical — don't miss it. Consider buying a small jar of Hungarian paprika or a bottle of pálinka (fruit brandy) as a budget souvenir from the market.

day_by_day.morning: Final Budapest Morning — Kazinczy Street & Coffee Culture: Enjoy a slow final morning in District VII. Have a proper Hungarian breakfast at a local étkezde. Browse the antique shops and bookstores along Király utca. Visit the Rumbach Street Synagogue (exterior) — a Moorish-style architectural gem. Pick up any last souvenirs at the nearby Gozsdu Udvar courtyard market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure Preparation & Transport: Depending on your flight or onward journey, head to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport via the 100E airport express bus (~€3, runs from Deák Ferenc tér every 20 minutes, ~35 minutes to airport). Alternatively, if returning to Prague, catch an afternoon RegioJet or FlixBus from Keleti station. Reflect on 8 incredible days across two of Central Europe's greatest cities.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or Overnight Travel: Board your flight or overnight train/bus. If departing late, enjoy one final langos or chimney cake at the airport or station.

meals.breakfast: Auguszt Cukrászda or a local neighborhood bakery — fresh pastry, rétes (apple strudel), and a strong espresso — budget ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Airport or station food — grab a sandwich and snack from a supermarket (Spar or Aldi near Keleti) before departing — budget ~€4–5
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or pack your own snacks for the journey home — budget ~€3–5

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for airport security at Budapest. The 100E bus is the cheapest reliable airport option — avoid taxi touts. Total estimated budget for the 8 days (excluding flights): accommodation ~€150–200, food ~€120–150, transport ~€50–70, attractions ~€80–100 — approximate total €400–520 per person, well within a budget-conscious travel style.

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 – no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Hradčany district boutique hotel via airport express bus (AE line) or taxi (~30 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a hotel map and neighborhood guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle neighborhood orientation walk around Hradčany. Stroll along Loretánská and Pohořelec streets, admire the exterior of Prague Castle complex and the Loreto pilgrimage site facade. Visit the peaceful Strahov Monastery garden terraces for panoramic views over the red rooftops of Malá Strana and the Old Town — a perfect low-effort first impression of Prague.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down the Castle Steps into Malá Strana (Lesser Town). Explore Nerudova Street lined with baroque townhouses, then cross the iconic Charles Bridge at dusk to watch the city lights reflect on the Vltava River. Return to Hradčany via tram.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Savoy in Malá Strana – elegant neo-Renaissance café offering Czech classics like svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and freshly baked pastries. Mid-range, ~400–600 CZK per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lokál Malá Strana – beloved local gastropub serving unpasteurized Pilsner Urquell tank beer and hearty Czech dishes like roast pork knee and potato dumplings. Lively atmosphere, ~350–550 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Keep luggage at the hotel and wear comfortable walking shoes. September in Prague is mild (15–20°C), so a light jacket for the evening is recommended. Validate your tram ticket before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex exploration (opens 9:00). Start with St. Vitus Cathedral – marvel at the Gothic spires, stained-glass windows by Alfons Mucha, and the Crown Jewels vault. Continue to the Old Royal Palace (Vladislav Hall) and the Basilica of St. George. Allow 2.5–3 hours for the full circuit. Book tickets online in advance to skip queues (~350 CZK for the full circuit).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through the Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička) – a row of tiny colorful medieval cottages where Franz Kafka briefly lived at No. 22. Exit toward Malá Strana and explore the ornate Wallenstein Garden (free entry), a baroque masterpiece with resident peacocks. Cross Charles Bridge again in daylight to study the 30 baroque statues up close.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Old Town (Staré Město). Watch the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour on Old Town Square. Climb the Old Town Hall Tower for a sunset panorama. Wander the Gothic lanes around Týn Church.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or grab fresh pastries and coffee at Eska Bakery near Florenc – renowned for sourdough and Czech-style open sandwiches.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Malostranská Beseda restaurant – traditional Czech cuisine in a historic building below the castle. Try the goulash with bread dumplings. ~300–500 CZK per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Čestr in Vinohrady or Mincovna on Old Town Square – quality Czech steakhouse with locally sourced beef, craft beers, and a buzzing atmosphere. ~500–700 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is the largest ancient castle complex in the world – wear very comfortable shoes. The castle grounds are free to enter; individual buildings require tickets. Arrive early (9:00–9:30) to beat tour groups. Tram lines 22 and 23 connect Hradčany directly to the castle area.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) – one of the best-preserved Jewish heritage sites in Europe. Tour the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Pinkas Synagogue (Holocaust memorial with 80,000 names inscribed on walls), the Spanish Synagogue (stunning Moorish interior), and the Maisel Synagogue. Combined ticket ~500 CZK. Allow 2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the river to Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhoods for a local, non-touristy Prague experience. Visit the Žižkov Television Tower (quirky communist-era structure with crawling baby sculptures by David Černý) and enjoy views from the observation deck. Explore the bohemian cafés and art nouveau apartment facades of Náměstí Míru square.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert or opera. Prague is renowned for affordable, high-quality performances – check the Estates Theatre (where Mozart premiered Don Giovanni in 1787) or the Municipal House (Art Nouveau gem). Tickets typically ~500–1,500 CZK for mid-range seats.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel. Alternatively, try Café Louvre near Národní třída – a grand 1902 café beloved by Kafka and Einstein, serving eggs, pastries, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Naše Maso butcher-deli in Josefov area – celebrated artisan butcher shop serving incredible open-faced sandwiches, tartare, and charcuterie boards. ~200–350 CZK.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Café Imperial – stunning Art Deco tiled interior, Czech-French cuisine. Try the duck confit or beef tartare. ~500–750 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter is closed on Saturdays. September 17 is a Thursday so no issue. Book concert tickets in advance via the venue websites. The Žižkov TV Tower has a one-room hotel suite inside if you're curious – worth a peek at the lobby.

day_by_day.morning: Half-day trip to Kutná Hora (1 hour by direct train from Prague's Hlavní nádraží, ~120 CZK each way). Visit the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) – a 15th-century chapel decorated with the bones of 40,000 people, including a chandelier containing every bone in the human body. Eerie, historic, and unforgettable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Kutná Hora to the stunning Cathedral of St. Barbara – a flamboyant Gothic masterpiece rivaling St. Vitus. Walk the medieval silver-mining town's cobblestone lanes and the Italian Court (former royal mint). Return train to Prague by 16:00–17:00.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed final Prague evening. Return to Charles Bridge and Malá Strana for a leisurely farewell stroll. Browse local craft shops on Nerudova Street for souvenirs (Bohemian crystal, garnets, marionettes). Enjoy a final Czech beer at a riverside terrace bar.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before catching the train (~8:00 departure recommended).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Restaurace Dačický – historic restaurant in a 16th-century building, serving medieval-inspired Czech cuisine. Try the roast boar or trout. ~350–500 CZK.
meals.dinner: Farewell Prague dinner at U Modré Kachničky (The Blue Duckling) in Malá Strana – intimate, romantic Czech restaurant specializing in game and duck dishes with excellent wine list. ~600–900 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check train times at cd.cz. The Kutná Hora train station is 2–3 km from the town center; take a local bus or taxi. Pack the Ossuary visit first as it opens at 8:00 and gets crowded by midday. This is your last full day in Prague – pack bags tonight for the Budapest journey tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Prague to Budapest. Take the RegioJet or Eurocity train from Praha Hlavní nádraží to Budapest Keleti – a scenic 6.5–7 hour journey through Czech and Slovak countryside (~800–1,500 CZK, book in advance). Depart ~8:00–9:00. Enjoy the views and bring snacks or use the dining car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Budapest Keleti station ~15:00–16:00. Transfer to your Budapest accommodation (hotel details not specified – recommend the VII District / Jewish Quarter or V District / Inner City for central access). Check in, freshen up. Take a short walk to get your bearings around the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: First Budapest impressions: Walk along the Danube Embankment on the Pest side at sunset. See the illuminated Hungarian Parliament Building (one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings). Stroll the Chain Bridge at dusk. The city's grand neo-Gothic and Baroque architecture is breathtaking at night.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel in Prague before departure, or grab a Trdelník pastry and coffee at the station.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the train or at a station stop in Brno or Bratislava (~20-min stop). Pack a picnic from a Prague deli or use the train dining car.
meals.dinner: Welcome Budapest dinner at Bors GasztroBar in the VII District – a legendary hole-in-the-wall serving creative, gourmet open-faced sandwiches and soups. Cult local favorite. ~2,000–3,500 HUF per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets at regiojet.com or cd.cz well in advance, especially for a Saturday. Store large luggage in overhead racks or luggage areas. The train passes through Brno and Bratislava – keep your passport handy as you cross into Hungary. Budapest uses Hungarian Forint (HUF); ATMs widely available at Keleti station.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle District (Várhegy). Take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) from Clark Ádám tér up to the castle hill (~1,200 HUF). Visit the Hungarian National Gallery inside Buda Castle, then walk to the Fisherman's Bastion – a fairy-tale neo-Romanesque terrace with seven turrets offering the most iconic panoramic views of Budapest and the Parliament across the Danube.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) – a stunning 13th-century Gothic church with a colorful diamond-patterned tiled roof, royal coronation site of Hungarian kings. Descend the castle hill via the medieval lanes of Úri utca and Tóth Árpád promenade. Cross the Chain Bridge on foot to Pest. Visit the grand St. Stephen's Basilica interior (free entry, ~200 HUF for tower access).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the famous Ruin Bars (Romkocsmák) of the VII District (Jewish Quarter). Start at Szimpla Kert – the original and most famous ruin bar, housed in a crumbling courtyard filled with eclectic furniture, street art, and live music. Vibrant, uniquely Budapest experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at New York Café (splurge option, one of the world's most beautiful cafés) or the more budget-friendly Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square for coffee and rétes (Hungarian strudel).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hungarikum Bisztró near the castle district – authentic Hungarian cuisine with gulyás (goulash), lángos (fried dough), and homemade pálinka. ~3,000–5,000 HUF per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mazel Tov in the Jewish Quarter – a stunning open-air ruin-bar-style restaurant serving Israeli-Mediterranean cuisine in a gorgeous garden setting. ~4,000–7,000 HUF per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a great day for Fisherman's Bastion as it's less crowded in the morning. The ruin bar scene starts late – Szimpla Kert fills up after 21:00. Wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestone castle district streets. Tram 2 along the Danube embankment offers spectacular views and is a sightseeing experience in itself.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building – one of Europe's largest and most ornate parliament buildings, a neo-Gothic masterpiece on the Danube bank. Guided tours run every 30–45 minutes (~6,000 HUF for non-EU visitors). See the Holy Crown of Hungary and the original coronation regalia. Book tickets online at jegy.parlament.hu.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) – Budapest's largest and most spectacular covered market, built in 1896. Browse stalls selling paprika, Hungarian salami, Tokaj wine, embroidered tablecloths, and folk art. Then walk the elegant Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's Champs-Élysées, UNESCO-listed) to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Millennium Monument.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Hungarian thermal bath. Visit Széchenyi Thermal Bath in City Park (open until 22:00) – Budapest's largest and most famous bath complex with 18 pools, steam rooms, and saunas in a stunning neo-Baroque yellow palace. Evening sessions are magical (~7,000–8,000 HUF). Bring or rent a towel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café Gerbeaud or a local pékség (bakery) – try a fresh kifli (crescent roll) with butter and Hungarian honey.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Great Market Hall upper floor food stalls – try lángos topped with sour cream and cheese, or a bowl of halászlé (fisherman's soup). ~1,500–2,500 HUF.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Onyx Restaurant (mid-range splurge) or Costes Downtown – both offer modern Hungarian fine dining with tasting menus showcasing local ingredients like Mangalica pork, foie gras, and Tokaj wine pairings. ~8,000–15,000 HUF per person.

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours sell out quickly – book at least 2–3 days ahead. The thermal bath evening session is a quintessential Budapest experience; Monday evenings are less crowded than weekends. Andrássy Avenue is walkable (~3 km from Parliament to Heroes' Square) or take Metro Line 1 (the oldest metro in continental Europe, opened 1896).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dohány Street Synagogue (Great Synagogue) – the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world, a stunning Moorish-Byzantine masterpiece. The complex includes a moving Holocaust memorial garden (the 'Weeping Willow' metal sculpture by Imre Varga) and the Jewish Museum. ~5,000 HUF, allow 1.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Budapest exploration: Walk through the elegant Inner City (V District) along Váci Street (pedestrian shopping street) to the Elizabeth Bridge viewpoint. Visit the Cave Church (Sziklatemplom) carved into Gellért Hill cliff face, then take the short hike or tram up Gellért Hill to the Citadella fortress for a final sweeping panorama of Budapest and the Danube with its five bridges.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and departure preparations. Pack, do a final souvenir shop for Hungarian paprika, Tokaj wine, Herend porcelain, or Rubik's Cubes (invented by Hungarian Ernő Rubik). Enjoy a last sunset Danube walk.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at your hotel or at the celebrated Auguszt Cukrászda patisserie – Budapest's oldest confectionery (est. 1870), serving exquisite Dobos torte (layered chocolate-caramel cake, a Hungarian invention) and Eszterházy cake.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Menza on Liszt Ferenc tér – stylish retro-communist-era design with modern Hungarian cuisine. Great value set lunch menu. ~3,500–5,500 HUF per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Stand25 Bisztró in the Great Market Hall area – celebrated restaurant by Michelin-starred chef Szabina Szulló, offering refined Hungarian bistro cuisine at accessible prices. ~6,000–10,000 HUF per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure logistics: Budapest Ferihegy Airport (BUD) is ~30–40 min by Airport Shuttle Bus 100E from Deák Ferenc tér (900 HUF). If flying next morning, ensure you're back at the hotel by 22:00. The Gellért Hill hike takes ~25 min on foot or you can take tram 19 to the base. This is a wonderful final day blending history, views, and gastronomy.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Václav Havel Airport to your boutique hotel in Hradčany district. Check-in, settle in, and refresh after the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the Hradčany neighborhood. Stroll along Hradčanské náměstí (Hradčany Square), admire the aristocratic palaces and baroque facades, and take in the sweeping panoramic views over the red-rooftop cityscape of Prague from the castle ramparts — no ticket required for the outer grounds. Visit the Loreto Shrine, a stunning baroque pilgrimage complex just steps from the hotel, featuring the Santa Casa and the Diamond Monstrance treasury.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour on the hotel terrace or a nearby wine bar in Hradčany. Dinner at Malý Buddha (Little Buddha) — an intimate, atmospheric restaurant near the castle serving refined Asian-inspired cuisine in a candlelit, incense-scented setting, perfect for a relaxed first evening.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments at the hotel upon check-in, or a charcuterie and wine spread at Café Savoy (short taxi ride, Malá Strana) — a grand Art Nouveau café with impeccable pastries and open-faced sandwiches.
meals.dinner: Malý Buddha, Hradčany — intimate, premium Asian cuisine; alternatively Lokál Hradčany for elevated Czech classics in a stylish setting. Budget approx. €60–90 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 begins only after 13:00 arrival. Keep the pace relaxed — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm hotel concierge has pre-arranged welcome amenities (champagne, seasonal fruit). Hradčany is walkable from the hotel for all afternoon stops.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) — the world's largest ancient castle complex, just minutes from the hotel. Begin with St. Vitus Cathedral (Gothic masterpiece, royal tombs, stained glass by Alfons Mucha), then the Old Royal Palace (Vladislav Hall), St. George's Basilica, and the Golden Lane — the charming row of tiny colorful houses once inhabited by castle guards and alchemists. Book a private guided tour for an in-depth historical narrative.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) via the Castle Steps. Explore the baroque gardens of the Wallenstein Palace and its peacock-filled garden. Cross the iconic Charles Bridge, pausing at each of the 30 baroque statues. Arrive in Staré Město (Old Town) — visit the Old Town Square, the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) on the hour for the mechanical procession, and the Church of Our Lady before Týn.
day_by_day.evening: Pre-dinner cocktails at the Terasa U Zlaté studně rooftop bar — arguably Prague's finest panoramic view over the city at golden hour. Dinner at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — a Michelin-starred restaurant in Old Town serving a refined tasting menu celebrating historic Bohemian recipes reimagined with modern technique. Reserve well in advance.

meals.breakfast: Elegant breakfast at the hotel — fresh pastries, cold cuts, eggs, fresh-pressed juices, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Café Savoy in Malá Strana — Art Nouveau grandeur, Czech open-faced sandwiches (chlebíčky), soups, and exceptional cakes. Budget approx. €25–40 per person.
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — Michelin-starred, 11-course tasting menu. Budget approx. €150–200 per person with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague Castle private guided tour and La Degustation well in advance. September weather is typically mild (15–20°C) — bring a light layer for the castle grounds. The walk from castle to Old Town is about 30–40 minutes and is one of Prague's great urban experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — one of the best-preserved Jewish heritage sites in Europe. Tour the Old Jewish Cemetery (layered with 12,000 graves), the Pinkas Synagogue (inscribed with 80,000 names of Czech Holocaust victims), the Spanish Synagogue (stunning Moorish interior), and the Maisel Synagogue. Engage a private guide for the full cultural and historical depth of this deeply moving neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Vinohrady and Žižkov districts — Prague's elegant late 19th-century residential neighborhoods. Stroll the leafy boulevards, admire the Art Nouveau and neo-baroque apartment buildings, and visit the Žižkov Television Tower (with its famous crawling baby sculptures by David Černý) for views over the city. Browse boutique design shops and antique galleries along Mánesova Street.
day_by_day.evening: Evening at the Prague State Opera or the Estates Theatre (Mozart premiered Don Giovanni here in 1787) — check the September 2027 program for opera, ballet, or classical concert. Pre-show dinner at Kampa Park, a legendary fine-dining restaurant perched on the Vltava riverbank beneath Charles Bridge, with a terrace perfect for a September evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with seasonal Czech fruits, artisan breads, and barista coffee.
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá in Old Town — beloved for its perfectly poured tank-fresh Pilsner Urquell and elevated Czech pub cuisine (svíčková, roast duck). Lively, authentic, and premium casual. Budget approx. €20–35 per person.
meals.dinner: Kampa Park — riverside fine dining, European cuisine with Czech accents, exceptional wine cellar. Budget approx. €80–120 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Book opera/theatre tickets as early as possible — September is peak cultural season. Josefov requires a combined ticket (approx. €20–25); private guide recommended for full context. Vinohrady is a 20-minute tram ride from Hradčany.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kutná Hora (1.5 hours from Prague by private transfer) — a UNESCO World Heritage medieval silver-mining town. Visit the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) — a small Gothic chapel decorated entirely with human bones arranged into chandeliers, coats of arms, and garlands. Then explore the magnificent Cathedral of Saint Barbara, one of Central Europe's finest Gothic cathedrals, with its soaring flying buttresses and remarkable frescoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll Kutná Hora's historic silver-mining town center — the Italian Court (former royal mint), the Stone Fountain, and the charming medieval streetscape. Return to Prague by private transfer in the late afternoon, arriving back in time to freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Prague evening — sunset walk across Charles Bridge and along the Vltava embankment. Dinner at Field Restaurant — a Michelin-starred contemporary Czech restaurant in Old Town, celebrated for its innovative farm-to-table tasting menus and outstanding natural wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — early start recommended for Kutná Hora.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Restaurace Dačický — a historic restaurant in a 16th-century building, serving hearty Bohemian cuisine (game, roast meats, local beers) in an atmospheric vaulted setting. Budget approx. €20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Field Restaurant, Prague Old Town — Michelin-starred tasting menu. Budget approx. €130–180 per person with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private driver for Kutná Hora day trip (approx. €120–180 round trip) for maximum comfort and flexibility. The Ossuary is a profound and unusual experience — not suitable for those sensitive to human remains. This is your last full Prague evening before transferring to Budapest.

day_by_day.morning: Final Prague morning — leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last stroll through Hradčany and the castle gardens (Královská zahrada — Royal Garden) if not yet visited, with its Renaissance Summer Palace and manicured grounds. Pack and check out; hotel concierge arranges luggage transfer to the station or airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium transfer Prague → Budapest. Options: Regiojet luxury train (approx. 7 hours, scenic Danube valley route — book a private compartment or First Class) or a short 1-hour flight (Czech Airlines / Wizz Air Business). Arrive Budapest late afternoon. Private transfer to your luxury hotel in Budapest (recommend the Buda Castle District or Pest's grand ring boulevard). Check in, freshen up, and take a first breathtaking look at the city.
day_by_day.evening: First Budapest evening — walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side for iconic views of Buda Castle, Chain Bridge, and Fisherman's Bastion illuminated at night. Dinner at Costes Restaurant — Budapest's first Michelin-starred restaurant, serving refined contemporary Hungarian cuisine in an elegant setting on Ráday Street.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast in Prague — unhurried and indulgent.
meals.lunch: Onboard dining (Regiojet First Class offers meal service) or airport lounge if flying. Alternatively, a packed gourmet picnic box arranged by the Prague hotel concierge.
meals.dinner: Costes Restaurant, Budapest — Michelin-starred, contemporary Hungarian tasting menu. Budget approx. €100–150 per person with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Book train or flight well in advance — September weekends are busy. If taking the train, the Prague–Budapest route through Slovakia and along the Danube is one of Europe's most scenic rail journeys. Arrange Budapest hotel private transfer in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Buda Castle Hill — cross the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) and ascend via the historic Castle Funicular (Budavári Sikló). Explore Buda Castle (Royal Palace), home to the Hungarian National Gallery (Baroque and 19th-century Hungarian masterworks) and the Budapest History Museum. Wander the medieval Castle District streets — Táncsics Mihály utca, Úri utca — and visit Matthias Church, a stunning Gothic church with diamond-patterned roof tiles and a lavishly decorated interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — the fairy-tale neo-Romanesque terrace offering Budapest's most iconic panoramic views over the Danube and the Parliament building. Descend to Víziváros (Watertown) and visit the Király Thermal Baths — one of Budapest's oldest Ottoman-era bathhouses (16th century). Enjoy a private thermal bath experience with a massage treatment for the ultimate luxury wellness afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Danube — book a private or small-group premium boat tour for the golden hour, watching the illuminated Parliament, Chain Bridge, and Castle Hill reflect on the river. Dinner at Onyx Restaurant — a Michelin-starred restaurant on Vörösmarty Square, celebrated for its theatrical Hungarian haute cuisine and impeccable service.

meals.breakfast: Grand hotel breakfast — Budapest's luxury hotels are renowned for lavish breakfast spreads.
meals.lunch: Ruszwurm Cukrászda in the Castle District — Budapest's oldest pastry shop (1827), perfect for a light lunch of open sandwiches, strudel, and coffee in a tiny, historic Biedermeier interior.
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant, Budapest — Michelin-starred, tasting menu. Budget approx. €140–190 per person with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Book Király Baths and massage in advance — Sunday is popular. The Danube sunset cruise should be reserved ahead; several luxury operators offer private charters. Fisherman's Bastion is free to access (inner terraces have a small fee); arrive early to beat crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Pest's grand boulevards and architectural treasures — begin at the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház), one of the world's most beautiful parliament buildings (Gothic Revival, 1902). Book a guided interior tour to see the Hungarian Crown Jewels, the main staircase, and the ornate debating chambers. Then walk to St. Stephen's Basilica (Szent István Bazilika) — Budapest's largest church, with a panoramic dome terrace and the relic of St. Stephen's mummified right hand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand Champs-Élysées-style boulevard, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House (one of Europe's most beautiful opera houses — take a guided tour of the interior even if not attending a performance). Continue to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) with its Millennium Monument, and stroll through Városliget (City Park), visiting the fairy-tale Vajdahunyad Castle. Optional: visit the Museum of Fine Arts on the square.
day_by_day.evening: Experience one of Budapest's legendary thermal bath palaces — the Széchenyi Thermal Baths in City Park, the largest medicinal bath in Europe (1913), for an evening bathing session as the sun sets over the neo-baroque building. Dinner at Borkonyha WineKitchen — a Michelin-starred restaurant specializing in Hungarian wines paired with refined seasonal Hungarian cuisine. Exceptional wine list with over 200 Hungarian labels.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most iconic historic coffeehouse (1858). Elegant lunch of Hungarian dishes, legendary cakes, and coffee in a grand salon setting. Budget approx. €25–40 per person.
meals.dinner: Borkonyha WineKitchen — Michelin-starred, Hungarian wine-focused tasting menu. Budget approx. €90–130 per person with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online in advance — morning slots sell out quickly. Széchenyi evening bathing (after 18:00) is a magical experience and less crowded than daytime. Bring a swimsuit and consider renting a private cabin for changing.

day_by_day.morning: Final Budapest morning — visit the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok), Budapest's magnificent 19th-century iron-and-brick market hall. Browse the ground floor for Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, artisan salami, foie gras, and hand-embroidered Kalocsa linen as premium souvenirs. Upper floor has traditional Hungarian food stalls — ideal for a final local breakfast of lángos (fried dough) or kürtőskalács (chimney cake). Stroll the Jewish Quarter (VII District) — visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (the largest in Europe), the Hungarian Jewish Museum, and the moving Raoul Wallenberg Memorial Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell luxury experience — book a final thermal spa session at the Gellért Thermal Baths, Budapest's most ornate Art Nouveau bathhouse (1918), with its stunning mosaic-tiled indoor pool. Alternatively, a private cooking class learning Hungarian classics (goulash, chicken paprikash, rétes strudel) with a renowned Budapest chef. Last stroll along the Danube Embankment and across the Liberty Bridge for a final view of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Costes Downtown — the sister restaurant of Costes, with a more relaxed but equally Michelin-starred menu, beautifully located on the Pest riverbank. Post-dinner, private transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport or hotel overnight for an early next-day departure. Toast to an extraordinary Eastern European journey.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel, then street food tasting at the Great Market Hall — lángos, fresh fruit, and Hungarian pastries.
meals.lunch: Gellért Hotel Restaurant — the legendary Art Nouveau hotel's dining room, serving classic Hungarian and international cuisine in a palatial setting overlooking the Danube. Budget approx. €40–60 per person.
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown — Michelin-starred, riverside fine dining. Budget approx. €100–150 per person with wine pairing. A fitting conclusion to a luxury cultural journey.

day_by_day.notes: Great Synagogue requires tickets in advance; closed on Saturdays (Shabbat) — Monday/Tuesday visits are ideal. Pack souvenirs carefully — Hungarian paprika and Tokaji Aszú wine make exceptional gifts. Confirm departure transfer timing with hotel concierge. Allow 2.5–3 hours before international flight departure from Budapest airport.
